title: Extended Duration Cargo Compartment Extinguishing Discharge for 240-Minute Diversion
abstract: Extension of the cargo compartment suppression discharge from 180 to 240 minutes by adding a third metering stage and re-balancing the distribution manifold, in support of longer overwater diversion times.

sections.reason: Three operators opening South Atlantic and mid-Pacific routings needed a 240-minute diversion approval, and the limiting item on this aircraft was the cargo compartment suppression duration rather than any propulsion or systems item. The existing installation meters the knock-down and the sustaining flow in two stages sized for 180 minutes. Rather than add bottle capacity, which costs weight and floor space, the change re-balances the distribution so that the sustaining concentration is held with less agent, and adds a third low-rate stage for the final hour.
sections.description: A third metering orifice stage is added downstream of the existing pair and the distribution manifold is re-balanced so that the forward and aft compartments reach the sustaining concentration within the same 45 seconds as before. The upper distribution pump D2620124013196 is re-worked with a smaller impeller, the aft distribution sensor D2620124813243 is replaced by a unit with a wider concentration range, and the forward heat exchanger D2620125756547 is deleted because the third stage runs cool enough not to need it. Nozzle positions are unchanged. The right-hand distribution switch 1394WF2, the left-hand heat exchanger position 58WF and the left-hand non-return valve position 6WF4 are all re-rated for the revised flow. Anchor nuts AES155061-5B and barrel nuts AES9630K5 secure the new orifice block and swaged collars LN413515-8E close the pipe joints. Work is in the cargo compartments and the belly fairing, zones 133, 142 and 183. Detail is on drawing D26200036707.
sections.effects: Mass reduction of 4.6 kg per aircraft because the deleted heat exchanger outweighs the added orifice block. No electrical load change. Not interchangeable: the third stage cannot be fitted without the re-balanced manifold and a mixed configuration would not hold the certified concentration. The change is a prerequisite for the 240-minute diversion approval and is stated as such in the aircraft flight manual supplement. The concentration test procedure in the AMM changes and the compartment must be re-tested after embodiment. No MMEL change; the dispatch conditions for the suppression system are unaltered.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in on the production line at MSN S01632 in October 2021. Retrofit is through Service Bulletin SLN-26-1009 and takes three days at a C-check, of which one day is the concentration test. Two aircraft in the range are excluded because they were converted to a different compartment lining standard.

title: Extended Duration Cargo Compartment Extinguishing Discharge for 240-Minute Diversion

issue.reason: An early coverage view for an insulated container in the bay is published, with the displaced volume and nozzle plane clearance a concept must respect.
